findings: IconProvider handles a missing requested file by File.Create at the system temporary directory plus the original basename. This can truncate an existing same-named temporary file, then delete it after icon extraction. No temporary file creation or Windows API was executed.
IconProvider does not check SHGetFileInfo return status before Icon.FromHandle. DestroyIcon and temporary-file deletion are not protected by finally, so extraction failures can skip cleanup.

ImageExtensions copies a System.Drawing.Bitmap and disposes the copy after conversion, but not its input; reviewed FileService callers do not dispose those returned provider bitmaps. Exception paths between LockBits and UnlockBits/Dispose have no finally here.

PreviewProvider does release HBITMAP through finally after conversion and uses finally to unlock both pixel buffers during copying. However destination LockBits requests ReadOnly while memcpy writes to it; no Windows runtime behavior claimed.

GetHBitmap releases the COM shell object after GetImage, without finally around cast/call. A thrown call can bypass release. Pixel copy assumes four source bytes per pixel for all formats at least 32 bits; actual shell formats and alpha semantics remain unqualified.

WindowService forwards window-style/context-menu requests through user32 without checking native return values. All reviewed P/Invoke declarations remain source-only; no native desktop integration run.
adoption: No upstream code adopted; resource ownership and bounded preview decoding remain relevant review criteria.
